paper: Kou (2002), 'A Jump-Diffusion Model for Option Pricing', Management Science 48(8):1086-1101 (with Kou & Wang 2004 companion on path-dependent options)

open_questions.q: Can Kou's own Hh-based Theorem 2 recursion (Appendix B.1) be implemented in a numerically stable way that reproduces C = 9.14732 at the footnote-9 parameters to at least 4 significant figures, without falling back to characteristic-function inversion?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md Section 2 (row C1'', 'attempted, failed') and Section 5 explicitly note that a literal transcription of the Hh backward recursion + I_n integral assembly diverged from the paper value by 20%+, and a public StackOverflow reference implementation is also wrong. The paper's specific implementation recipe --- as opposed to its price --- is thus not independently vetted. The failure mode is consistent with well-known instability of Hh_n backward recursion for large negative arguments, but this has not been isolated or fixed here.
next_steps: Re-derive the Hh recursion symbolically and identify the direction of numerical stability (forward vs backward, and for which argument regime).
Implement Hh_n using an asymptotic series or continued-fraction expansion for large |x| instead of pure recursion.
Cross-check the I_n(c; alpha, beta, delta) integral assembly against a high-precision numerical quadrature (mpmath, prec=100) to isolate whether the discrepancy is in Hh_n or in I_n.
Compare the corrected Hh implementation against the COS answer 9.147317 --- agreement at 1e-6 would independently vet Kou's specific closed-form recipe.

open_questions.q: How does the closed-form European price generalise --- and how does it compare against the Kou-Wang (2004) Laplace-transform pricer --- for path-dependent options (American, barrier, lookback) under the same double-exponential jump-diffusion, and does the Laplace-inversion route match Monte Carlo at benchmark parameters?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md Preamble notes that the assignment header referenced Kou & Wang (2004) but the European closed-form actually lives in Kou (2002); the 2004 companion paper covers Laplace-transform pricing of American / path-dependent options under the same model. This replication tests only the European call; no path-dependent option has been priced or cross-checked, so the 2004 paper's core contribution is entirely untested here.
next_steps: Implement a Monte-Carlo pricer for a down-and-out barrier option under the Kou SDE (exact log-price simulation is already in run_replication.py; add a per-step barrier check via Brownian-bridge correction or fine time discretisation).
Implement the Kou-Wang (2004) Laplace-transform pricer for the same barrier option and invert numerically (e.g. Gaver-Stehfest or Euler algorithm).
Compare on a benchmark parameter grid; agreement within MC error would independently replicate the 2004 paper's central claim.
Extend to American puts via the Kou-Wang first-passage-to-optimal-boundary formulation.

open_questions.q: Does the double-exponential jump-diffusion actually fit observed equity-index option smiles better than the Merton normal-jump model (and than Heston stochastic volatility) on real market data, as motivated in Kou (2002), and how do the calibrated jump parameters (lambda, eta_1, eta_2, p) shift across pre/post-2020 regimes?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md Section 5 explicitly flags: 'No empirical / volatility-smile claims tested. The paper motivates the double-exponential model by its ability to fit observed leptokurtic returns and implied-volatility smiles. This replication tests only the mathematical/pricing claims. No historical returns were downloaded, no smile was calibrated, no comparison against Merton or Heston fits on real option data was made.' The paper's practical appeal is thus entirely open.
next_steps: Pull a public SPX option-chain snapshot (e.g. from CBOE or WRDS academic access) for a set of expiries.
Calibrate Kou (5 params: sigma, lambda, eta_1, eta_2, p) by least-squares on implied vol across strikes, using the existing COS pricer.
Calibrate Merton (3 params: sigma, lambda, mu_J, sigma_J) and Heston (5 params) as head-to-head baselines.
Compare RMSE-in-implied-vol across strike ranges; report separately for pre-2020, 2020 COVID stress, and post-2022 regimes to check parameter stability.

open_questions.q: Does a converged PIDE solver (Crank-Nicolson time + implicit or FFT jump-kernel convolution + Richardson extrapolation) push the finite-difference route from ~2e-2 agreement (current explicit-Euler baseline) down to ~1e-4 or better, and does that hold across the strike sweep?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md Section 5 flags: 'PIDE agreement is only at O(1e-2) ... consistent with the coarse-ish grid (Nx=601, dx ~ 8.3e-3) and explicit-Euler time-stepping, but it is not tight enough to independently distinguish e.g. a sign error in the drift correction -lambda*zeta from a ~1% discretisation artefact.' The current PIDE result (9.16756 vs paper 9.14732) is a plausibility check rather than a true independent third witness.
next_steps: Replace explicit Euler with Crank-Nicolson (implicit diffusion) + implicit or explicit-Fourier convolution for the jump integral (IMEX scheme).
Replace the dense Nx x Nx jump-kernel matrix with an FFT-based convolution on a periodic-extended grid to allow much finer x-grids at O(N log N).
Do a Richardson extrapolation study in dx and dt jointly; expected observed order should be 2 for CN and consistent with the truncation analysis.
Report convergence tables at K in {90, 95, 100, 105, 110}; a successful test is |PIDE - COS| < 1e-4 uniformly across strikes.

open_questions.q: Does the double-exponential jump-diffusion extend cleanly to multi-asset baskets (e.g. two-asset spread options or basket calls) with correlated Brownian components and a shared/asymmetric jump-arrival process, and can COS-2D (or a 2D characteristic-function inversion) price such contracts accurately against Monte Carlo?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md Section 5 flags 'only one parameter set is exercised' and 'no sweep over lambda, jump asymmetry, or tail parameters was performed.' Multi-asset extension is not addressed at all in the current replication. Practitioners routinely need basket / spread-option pricers, and whether Kou's tractability survives correlated-jump generalisation is an open modelling question with real payoff.
next_steps: Formulate a two-asset Kou model: correlated Brownian motions (correlation rho) plus a shared Poisson clock with per-asset asymmetric double-exponential jumps (allowing marginal fits).
Derive the joint characteristic function of (log S1_T, log S2_T); it should remain closed-form given the double-exponential's memoryless property.
Implement 2D COS (Ruijter-Oosterlee 2012) for a spread-option payoff max(S1 - S2 - K, 0) and cross-check against 2M-path Monte Carlo on 3-5 correlation/jump-asymmetry configurations.
Investigate whether an idiosyncratic-jump variant (independent Poisson processes per asset) is analytically as tractable, or whether one loses the closed-form character.
